models_evaluated: DLHD (deep learning-based intracranial hemorrhage detection algorithm)

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance and decision consistency for intracranial hemorrhage without versus with AI, by experience level
links.effect: Experienced participants were minimally affected. Inexperienced participants' sensitivity rose 59.33% to 72.67% and specificity fell 65.49% to 53.73% (both p<0.001), with decision changes driven mainly by AI false positives.
links.quote: In contrast, inexperienced participants exhibited significantly increased sensitivity (59.33-72.67%, p < 0.001) and decreased specificity (65.49-53.73%, p < 0.001) with the algorithm.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the impact of providing AI assistance versus unassisted clinician interpretation of brain CT scans in a simulated clinical workflow.
